translationRepairs: Wen set out wine for his mother, very merry, and speaking of family affairs said to her: "Zhu Five Classics toiled at Confucian learning yet never received a single appointment; now I have a son who is military commissioner—no disgrace to our forebears!"

Wen set out wine for his mother, very merry, and speaking of family affairs said to her: "Zhu Five Classics toiled at Confucian learning yet never received a single appointment; now there is a son who is military commissioner—no disgrace to our forebears!"

Focus speech 今有子為節度使 means Zhu Five Classics now has a son who is jiedushi (Wen of himself); the prior literal's "I have a son who is military commissioner" invents Wen as that son's father. Mother's reply in s0023 (汝致身及此) confirms Wen is the risen son. The proposed wording restores the correct kinship without new error.

sourceDate.text: 乾化二年十一月二十三日

units.zh: 文惠皇太后王氏，開平初追諡。
units.en: Empress Dowager Wenhui (Wang) received her posthumous title early in the Kaiping era.
units.literal: Empress Dowager Wenhui, née Wang, was given a posthumous title at the beginning of Kaiping.

units.zh: 太祖性孝願，奉太后未嘗小失色，朝夕視膳，為士君子之規範。
units.en: The Founder was deeply filial: he never let his manner slip before the Empress Dowager and attended her at every meal, morning and night—a standard for the cultivated man.
units.literal: The Founder by nature was filial and reverent; in serving the Empress Dowager he never once showed the slightest lapse of countenance, morning and evening attending her meals—a model for gentlemen and scholars.

units.zh: 帝嚴察用法，無纖毫假貸，太后言之，帝頗為省刑。
units.en: The Emperor enforced the law without mercy; when the Empress Dowager intervened, he often eased sentences.
units.literal: The Emperor was strict in investigation and application of law, granting not the slightest indulgence; when the Empress Dowager spoke of it, the Emperor considerably lightened punishments.

units.zh: 〈（《北夢瑣言》云：梁祖父誠蚤卒，有三子俱幼。
units.en: (The 《Scattered Dreams of the Northern Quarter》 records that the Liang founder’s father Cheng died early, with three sons still small.
units.literal: (《Scattered Dreams of the Northern Quarter》 says: The Liang Founder’s father Cheng died young, leaving three sons all still young.

units.zh: 母王氏，攜養寄於同縣人劉崇家。
units.en: Their mother Wang entrusted the boys to Liu Chong, a man of the same county.
units.literal: The mother, née Wang, took them to be raised and lodged with Liu Chong of the same county.

units.zh: 昆弟之中，惟溫狡猾無行，崇母撫養之，崇兄弟嘗加譴杖。
units.en: Of the brothers only Wen was sly and unruly; Liu Chong’s mother cared for him, while Chong’s brothers often thrashed him.
units.literal: Among the brothers, only Wen was cunning and without proper conduct; Chong’s mother raised him, and Chong’s brothers sometimes beat him with rods.

units.zh: 一日，偷崇家釜而竄，為崇追回，崇母遮護，以免撲責。
units.en: Once he stole a pot from the Chong household and ran; caught and dragged back, he was spared the rod only because Chong’s mother stood between him and punishment.
units.literal: One day he stole a cauldron from Chong’s house and fled; Chong caught him and brought him back, but Chong’s mother shielded him so he escaped a beating.

units.zh: 善逐走鹿，往往及而獲之。
units.en: He could run down deer on foot and usually brought them down.
units.literal: He was skilled at chasing running deer and often overtook and caught them.

units.zh: 又，崇母常見其有龍蛇之異。
units.en: Liu Chong’s mother also claimed to see dragon-and-serpent portents about him.
units.literal: Moreover, Chong’s mother often saw in him omens of dragons and serpents.

units.zh: 他日與仲兄存入黃巢軍作賊，伯兄昱與母王氏尚依劉家。
units.en: Later Wen and his second brother Cun went off with Huang Chao’s rebels; the eldest, Yu, and Mother Wang remained with the Lius.
units.literal: Another day he and his second brother Cun joined Huang Chao’s army as bandits; the eldest brother Yu and their mother Wang still relied on the Liu household.

units.zh: 溫既辭去，不知存亡。
units.en: After Wen departed, his fate was unknown.
units.literal: Once Wen had left, none knew whether he lived or died.

units.zh: 及溫領鎮於汴，盛飾輿馬，使人迎母於崇家。
units.en: When Wen became military governor at Bian, he sent a splendid escort to bring his mother from the Chong home.
units.literal: When Wen held command at Bian, he lavishly adorned carriage and horses and sent men to welcome his mother from Chong’s house.

units.zh: 王氏惶恐，辭避深藏，不之信，謂人曰：「朱三落拓無行，何處作賊送死，焉能自致富貴？
units.en: Wang was afraid, refused, and hid; she told others: "That good-for-nothing Zhu Third is off robbing somewhere—how could he possibly have become rich and powerful?
units.literal: Wang was terrified, declined, and hid deep away, not believing it, and said to people: "Zhu Third is shiftless and without conduct—where is he playing bandit and courting death, that he could enrich himself and rise to nobility?

units.zh: 汴帥非吾子也。」
units.en: The lord of Bian cannot be my boy."
units.literal: The Bian commander is not my son."

units.zh: 使者具陳離鄉去裏之由，歸國立功之事，王氏方泣而信。
units.en: The envoy explained how Wen had left home, served the dynasty, and won distinction; at last Wang wept and believed.
units.literal: The messenger fully set forth the reasons for leaving home and native place and the deeds of returning to the state and achieving merit; only then did Wang weep and believe.

units.zh: 是日，與崇母並迎歸汴。
units.en: The same day both mothers were brought to Bian.
units.literal: That day she and Chong’s mother were both welcomed back to Bian.

units.zh: 溫盛禮郊迎，人士改觀。
units.en: Wen met them with full suburban ceremony, and onlookers saw him in a new light.
units.literal: Wen received them with grand rites at the suburban greeting; gentlemen changed their view of him.

units.zh: 崇以舊恩，位至列卿，為商州刺史。
units.en: For past kindness to the family, Chong rose to a chief-ministerial post and served as prefect of Shang.
units.literal: Chong, because of old kindness, rose to rank among chief ministers and became prefect of Shangzhou.

units.zh: 王氏以溫貴，封晉國太夫人。
units.en: With Wen’s rise, Wang was created Grand Lady of Jin.
units.literal: Because Wen had become noble, Wang was enfeoffed as Grand Lady of Jin.

units.zh: 仲兄存，於賊中為矢石所中而卒。
units.en: The second brother Cun died in the rebel ranks, killed by missile weapons.
units.literal: The second brother Cun, in the bandit army, was struck by arrow and stone and died.

units.zh: 溫置酒於母，歡甚，語及家事，謂母曰：「朱五經辛苦業儒，不登一命，今有子為節度使，無忝前人矣！」
units.en: At a feast for his mother Wen grew merry and said: "Father Zhu Five Classics studied the classics in poverty and never won office—yet his son is now a military commissioner. We have not shamed our ancestors!"
units.literal: Wen set out wine for his mother, very merry, and speaking of family affairs said to her: "Zhu Five Classics toiled at Confucian learning yet never received a single appointment; now there is a son who is military commissioner—no disgrace to our forebears!"

units.zh: 母不懌，良久謂溫曰：「汝致身及此，信為英特，行義未必如先人。
units.en: His mother was unmoved and after a pause told Wen: "You have risen high—no doubt you are gifted—but your conduct is hardly like your father’s.
units.literal: His mother was displeased and after a long while said to Wen: "You have reached this station—truly you are extraordinary—but in conduct you surely do not match your forebears.

units.zh: 朱二與汝同入賊軍，身死蠻徼，孤男稚女，艱食無告。
units.en: Your brother Zhu Second went into the rebels with you and died on the frontier; his widow and children are destitute, with no one to help them.
units.literal: Zhu Second entered the bandit army with you and died on the barbarian frontier; orphaned boys and young girls eat bitterly with none to plead for them.

units.zh: 汝未有恤孤之心，英特即有，諸無取也。」
units.en: You show no care for his orphans. Talent alone is nothing to boast of."
units.literal: You have not the heart to succor orphans—if you are extraordinary, still do not take pride in it."

units.zh: 溫垂涕謝罪，即令召諸兄子皆至汴。
units.en: Wen wept and apologized, then had every nephew brought to Bian.
units.literal: Wen shed tears and apologized, and at once ordered all his brothers’ sons summoned to Bian.

units.zh: 友寧、友倫皆立軍功，位至方鎮。）〉
units.en: Youning and Youlun both won military honors and rose to govern provinces.)〉
units.literal: Youning and Youlun both established military merit and reached posts as regional commissioners.)〉

units.zh: 元貞皇后張氏，乾化中追諡。
units.en: Empress Yuanzhen (Zhang) was posthumously honored during Qianhua.
units.literal: Empress Yuanzhen, née Zhang, was given a posthumous title in the Qianhua era.

units.zh: 〈（《五代會要》云：太祖皇后張氏早崩，開平二年，追封賢妃，至乾化二年十一月二十三日，追冊曰元貞皇后。
units.en: (The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 records that Empress Zhang died young; in Kaiping 2 she was posthumously made Worthy Consort, and on 23 xi of month 11, Qianhua 2, was elevated to Empress Yuanzhen.
units.literal: (《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 says: The Founder’s empress Zhang died early; in Kaiping year 2 she was posthumously enfeoffed as Worthy Consort; on the twenty-third day of the eleventh month of Qianhua year 2 she was posthumously invested as Empress Yuanzhen.

units.zh: 又，《北夢瑣言》云：梁祖魏國夫人張氏，碭山富室女，父蕤，曾為宋州刺史。
units.en: The 《Scattered Dreams of the Northern Quarter》 adds that Lady Zhang of Wei came from a rich Dangshan family; her father Rui had served as Songzhou prefect.
units.literal: Moreover, 《Scattered Dreams of the Northern Quarter》 says: The Liang Founder’s Lady of Wei, née Zhang, was daughter of a wealthy house in Dangshan; her father Rui had once been prefect of Song.

units.zh: 溫時聞張有姿色，私心傾慕，有麗華之歎。
units.en: Hearing of Zhang’s beauty, Wen secretly yearned for her and sighed like a man longing for Lady Lihua.
units.literal: When Wen heard that Zhang had beauty, he secretly admired her and sighed with the lament of Lady Lihua.

units.zh: 及溫在同州，得張於兵間，因以婦禮納之。
units.en: At Tongzhou Wen took Zhang from among the captives and married her properly.
units.literal: When Wen was at Tongzhou he obtained Zhang amid the troops and took her in with the rites of a wife.

units.zh: 溫以其宿款，深加禮異。
units.en: Wen had loved her long before; he honored her with exceptional ceremony.
units.literal: Because of his long-standing affection, Wen treated her with deep courtesy and distinction.

units.zh: 張賢明有禮，溫雖虎狼其心，亦所景伏。
units.en: Zhang was intelligent and decorous; even Wen’s brutal nature bowed before her.
units.literal: Zhang was wise, clear, and observant of ritual; though Wen had the heart of a wolf or tiger, toward her he also bowed in awe.

units.zh: 每軍謀國計，必先延訪。
units.en: On every matter of war or statecraft he consulted her first.
units.literal: Whenever there was military planning or state policy, he first extended invitation to consult her.

units.zh: 或已出師，中途有所不可，張氏一介請旋，如期而至，其信重如此。
units.en: If a campaign had to be recalled mid-march, a single word from Zhang brought the army back on time—such was her authority.
units.literal: Even after the army had marched out, if midway something could not proceed, Zhang with a single message would request return—and arrived on the appointed day; such was the trust placed in her.

units.zh: 初收兗、鄆，得朱瑾妻，溫告之曰：「彼既無依，寓於輜車。」
units.en: After the capture of Yan and Yun they took Zhu Jin’s wife; Wen told her: "She has no one to rely on—let her travel in the supply train."
units.literal: When Yan and Yun were first taken, they obtained Zhu Jin’s wife; Wen told her: "She has no one to rely on—let her lodge in the baggage train."

units.zh: 張氏遣人召之，瑾妻再拜，張氏答拜泣下，謂之曰：「兗、鄆與司空同姓之國，昆仲之間，以小故尋戈，致吾姒如此。
units.en: Zhang sent for her; Jin’s wife bowed low, Zhang bowed back in tears and said: "Yan and Yun share our house’s surname—brothers quarreled over a trifle, and you, my sister-in-law, suffer for it.
units.literal: Zhang sent someone to summon her; Jin’s wife bowed twice, Zhang returned the bow weeping, and said to her: "Yan and Yun are states of the same surname as the Minister of Works; between brothers a small quarrel drew swords, and my sister-in-law has come to this.

units.zh: 設不幸汴州失守，妾亦似吾姒之今日也。」
units.en: Should Bian fall, I would share your fate."
units.literal: If by misfortune Bianzhou should fall, I too would be as my sister-in-law is today."

units.zh: 又泣下，乃度為尼，張恒給其費。
units.en: Weeping again, she had Jin’s wife take the veil and paid her upkeep.
units.literal: Again she wept, then had her tonsured as a nun; Zhang constantly supplied her expenses.

units.zh: 張既卒，繼寵者非人，及僭號後，大縱朋淫，骨肉聚麀，帷薄荒穢，以致友珪之禍，起於婦人。
units.en: After Zhang’s death Wen’s favorites were unworthy; once emperor he plunged into orgies and incest until Yougui’s revolt—born of a woman’s grievance.
units.literal: After Zhang died, those who succeeded her in favor were not worthy; after he assumed the imperial title he greatly indulged debauchery with companions, kin coupled like beasts, curtains and screens foul—so that Yougui’s disaster arose from a woman.

units.zh: 始能以柔婉之德，製豺虎之心，如張氏者，不亦賢乎！
units.en: At first, with soft grace she tamed a tiger’s heart—was Zhang not truly virtuous?
units.literal: To begin with, by gentle and yielding virtue to restrain the heart of wolf and tiger—as with Zhang—is she not worthy?

units.zh: 又，案《五代會要》所載，內職有梁太祖昭儀陳氏、昭容李氏，《歐陽史》並見《家人傳》。）〉
units.en: The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 also lists the Founder’s Lady of Bright Deportment Chen and Lady of Bright Countenance Li, both noted in Ouyang Xiu’s 《New History》 Family section.)〉
units.literal: Moreover, examining what the 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 records, among inner offices were the Founder’s Lady of Bright Deportment Chen and Lady of Bright Countenance Li; both appear in 《Ouyang’s History》 in the Family Biographies.)〉

units.zh: 末帝德妃張氏。
units.en: Virtue Consort Zhang, consort of the Last Emperor.
units.literal: The Last Emperor’s Virtue Consort, née Zhang.

units.zh: 〈（《五代會要》云：少帝妃張氏，乾化五年九月二十四日，冊為德妃，其夕薨。
units.en: (The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 records that the Young Emperor’s consort Zhang was created Virtue Consort on 24 ix, Qianhua 5, and died the same night.
units.literal: (《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 says: The Young Emperor’s consort Zhang, on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month of Qianhua year 5, was invested as Virtue Consort; that very evening she died.

units.zh: 案《歐陽史次妃郭氏傳》云：晉天福三年，詔太社先藏罪人首級，許親屬收葬，乃出末帝首，遣右衛將軍安崇阮與妃同葬。
units.en: Ouyang’s 《History》 biography of Consort Guo notes that in Tianfu 3 Jin permitted families to claim criminals’ heads from the Grand Altar; the Last Emperor’s head was released and General An Chongruan buried it with his consort.
units.literal: Examining 《Ouyang’s History》, in the biography of the second consort Guo it says: In Jin Tianfu year 3 an edict allowed kin to bury heads of criminals long stored at the Grand Altar; the Last Emperor’s head was produced, and Right Palace Guard general An Chongruan was sent to bury it together with the consort.

units.zh: 妃卒洛陽。
units.en: She died at Luoyang.
units.literal: The consort died at Luoyang.

units.zh: 又案：《五代史》無外戚傳。
units.en: The 《History of the Five Dynasties》 contains no treatise on imperial in-laws.
units.literal: Moreover, examining: 《History of the Five Dynasties》 has no biography of maternal kin.

units.zh: 《五代會要》云：梁太祖長女安陽公主，降羅廷規，開平二年八月追封。
units.en: The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 lists the Founder’s eldest daughter, Princess Anyang, married to Luo Tinggui and posthumously enfeoffed in Kaiping 2, month 8.
units.literal: 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 says: The Founder’s eldest daughter, Princess of Anyang, was married to Luo Tinggui and posthumously enfeoffed in Kaiping year 2, eighth month.

units.zh: 長樂公主，降趙岩，開平元年五月十一日封。
units.en: Princess Changle wed Zhao Yan and was enfeoffed on 11 v, Kaiping 1.
units.literal: Princess of Changle was married to Zhao Yan and enfeoffed on the eleventh day of the fifth month of Kaiping year 1.

units.zh: 普寧公主，降昭祚王氏，開平元年五月十一日封。
units.en: Princess Puning wed Wang Zhaozuo on the same date, 11 v, Kaiping 1.
units.literal: Princess of Puning was married to Wang Zhaozuo and enfeoffed on the eleventh day of the fifth month of Kaiping year 1.

units.zh: 金華公主，開平二年十月封。
units.en: Princess Jinhua was enfeoffed in month 10, Kaiping 2.
units.literal: Princess of Jinhua was enfeoffed in the tenth month of Kaiping year 2.

units.zh: 真寧公主，乾化三年十月五日封。
units.en: Princess Zhenning was enfeoffed on 5 x, Qianhua 3.
units.literal: Princess of Zhenning was enfeoffed on the fifth day of the tenth month of Qianhua year 3.

units.zh: 少帝長女壽春公主，乾化三年四月五日封。
units.en: The Young Emperor’s eldest, Princess Shouchun, was enfeoffed on 5 iv, Qianhua 3.
units.literal: The Young Emperor’s eldest daughter, Princess of Shouchun, was enfeoffed on the fifth day of the fourth month of Qianhua year 3.

units.zh: 第二女壽昌公主，貞明元年九月二十三日封。
units.en: His second daughter, Princess Shouchang, was enfeoffed on 23 ix, Zhenming 1.
units.literal: His second daughter, Princess of Shouchang, was enfeoffed on the twenty-third day of the ninth month of Zhenming year 1.

units.zh: 今考《通鑒考異》引《梁功臣列傳》云：羅廷規尚安陽公主，又尚金華公主。
units.en: The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 collation cites the 《Biographies of Liang Meritorious Officials》: Luo Tinggui married both Princess Anyang and Princess Jinhua.
units.literal: Now examining 《Comprehensive Mirror: Collation of Variants》, which cites 《Biographies of Liang Meritorious Officials》: Luo Tinggui married Princess of Anyang and also married Princess of Jinhua.

units.zh: 《薛史羅紹威傳》亦載開平四年，詔金華公主出家為尼。
units.en: The 《Old History》 biography of Luo Shaowei likewise records an edict in Kaiping 4 ordering Princess Jinhua to take the veil.
units.literal: 《Xue History》, biography of Luo Shaowei, also records that in Kaiping year 4 an edict had Princess of Jinhua leave the world and become a nun.

units.zh: 是金華公主實歸羅氏，而《五代會要》不載亦闕文也。）〉
units.en: So Jinhua truly married into the Luo house, though the 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 omits it—another gap in the record.)〉
units.literal: Thus Princess of Jinhua in fact went to the Luo clan, while the 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 does not record it—again a lacuna in the text.)〉

candidatePacket.instructions: Review dates, event ownership, conversions, endpoint evidence, age reckoning, omitted life dates, and active-date hints. Read all Chinese units for omissions; English is not independent evidence. Do not re-extract names or mentions. For each item identify whose event is dated and justify each endpoint. Same mother does not imply same birth year. Later allusions are not personal activity. Research or record a blocker rather than invent precision. A report cannot approve with missing checks or unresolved research.

validation.exactAtomicScope: PASS: 57 audit-named temporal claim or active-hint repairs; no names, roles, mentions, relationships, source, or translation fields changed.
validation.preservedEvidence: PASS: source facts remain in source-faithful undated attestations or in existing direct honors, deaths, and events.

findings.problem: Posthumous and relative dates were converted into personal activity
findings.action: Keep the explicit posthumous honors and their Chinese date wording, but delete duplicate living attestations and active hints; remove any unverified exact Western point from 開平初 or 以溫貴.

findings.problem: Rebellion, dynasty, and reign windows were assigned as person-specific activity
findings.action: Remove the interval-bearing attestations and matching active hints. Retain the underlying undated deaths, offices, kinship, capture, and title facts without inventing endpoints.

findings.problem: Undated allusions and bibliographical references were treated as exact personal dates
findings.action: Preserve the source text and bibliographical references, but remove the exact personal Western-date claims and matching hints unless an independently cited source establishes them.

findings.problem: Later burial and spouse/princess events were attributed to the wrong person
findings.action: Preserve the AD 938 burial authorization and the direct princess honors as their own events. Remove the misplaced Last Emperor/Consort Guo and spouses’ activity dates; retain only genuinely direct evidence such as the Last Emperor’s AD 915 consort record.
